prize_parts.citation: for first-principles molecular dynamics, unifying electronic-structure calculation with the motion of atoms

statement.case_for: After reading all eight opening ballots I move Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics from my third place to my preferred single-achievement prize. It is the only shortlisted candidacy that combines a clear physical principle (an extended Lagrangian coupling electrons and nuclei), a clean two-author attribution (the 1985 paper) and four decades of independent adoption with a stable interpretation. It already has two first-place votes (Aqvist, Linke) and sits in my top three. It makes proton transfer, bond breaking and condensed-phase chemistry computable from first principles, which touches my own field of biological energy conversion indirectly. As Secretary, I also note that a candidacy resting on one dated, attributable discovery is much easier to defend in the expert report than one resting on a broad line of work.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is subfield and field-boundary: the method lies close to condensed-matter physics and the same tools (DFT, ab initio MD) have been recognized adjacent to it (Kohn-Pople 1998, the 2013 multiscale prize). Parrinello's later metadynamics work might be seen as the more chemical contribution, and a committee could ask whether the original achievement has already been partly credited elsewhere. The prize would also be purely theory and method, with no experimental or biological counterpart, so it gives less of a chemistry-wide signal than a prize that bridges to life science.

responses.point: Car-Parrinello is a clean two-person credit with four decades of adoption, a true game-changer for theory that connects quantitatively to experiment, and recognition is overdue.
responses.response: I agree on attribution and maturity. Where I would qualify your case is the claim that the later work is not needed: for the citation I would anchor strictly on the 1985 unification of electronic structure and ionic motion, and ask the expert report to confirm that the later plane-wave and Born-Oppenheimer variants do not blur priority. In terms of experimental connection, I would want the report to cite concrete cases, such as proton transfer in water and in enzyme active sites, rather than rely on general impact.

responses.point: Massively parallel sequencing deserves to be first, with Balasubramanian and Klenerman as the chemical core of the Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry, and recognition is overdue.
responses.response: The impact is beyond doubt and I do not dispute maturity. My difficulty is attribution: five credited names across competing chemistries (reversible terminators, pyrosequencing, clonal arrays), and Sanger sequencing was recognized in 1980. A pair limited to Balasubramanian and Klenerman leaves out Rothberg's platform, which Linke and Aili both include, so the committee would be choosing among routes more than recognizing one discovery. I regard it as my second alternative, not as the first choice, unless the expert report resolves which route is decisive.

responses.point: Car-Parrinello puts electronic structure and nuclear motion into one extended Lagrangian, is a clear physical idea turned into a chemical tool, and has a clean 1985 attribution.
responses.response: I concur, and as a trained physicist I share your appreciation of the principle. I do not share the assumption that cleanliness of attribution alone justifies being first. I would test it against Aili's and Aqvist's competing arguments for the lipid and degrader candidacies, where societal impact is larger but credit is contested, and I think a two-person prize with no attribution risk is the safer decision, not necessarily the more important one.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry for siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, with the Vancouver group (Cullis, Hope, Madden) as the core.
responses.response: The consequences are enormous, but the credit is spread across at least six names and academic and company teams, and your own ballot concedes that the Vancouver versus MIT split is disputed. I also doubt that the committee should treat formulation of this kind as the central chemical achievement while the 2023 Medicine prize is still recent. I would need the expert report to establish priority in ionizable lipid design before I could support a specific three-person list.

responses.point: Molecular-sieve and zeolite design (Corma, Davis, Zones) is a clear case of structure determining function, with decades of confirmation and industrial deployment.
responses.response: I accept that the evidence is rigorous and mature, and I defer to your expertise on framework structure. My concern is that this candidacy is a line of work over many years more than a single attributable discovery, and Tsapatsis and Yu are only partly separated from the trio, so the three-name limit is binding. It received only one first-place vote, and I would like the expert report to specify which design principle is the decisive one.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report will treat Car-Parrinello as chemistry rather than physics, and whether earlier recognition of DFT and multiscale methods makes the committee hesitant.
Gray and Winkler (B068) have only my opening vote, so it is unclear whether my own field interest is shared; priority relative to Marcus-type theory also needs checking.
Whether the committee prefers a two-part prize pairing a method with a mechanism, which the three-person limit makes difficult given that B024 already uses two names.
statement.conflict_note: I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, whose first-ranked candidacy (B030) is not my preferred pick, and I work in biological electron and proton transfer, which could be seen as touching B068 (Gray, Winkler) as an alternative. No specific conflict is apparent for B024.
